he accepted from them on the condition that no one should ever remain in it.
And all those who were hidden came out,
and they were dispersed throughout the lands,
and it was completely emptied of inhabitants.
Guards were appointed, however, who prevented the Ghuzz from doing harm to those who were departing.
Now all of this happened because of the insults that the people of Sinjar cast at the Ghuzz when they had fled at first before the Ma'addites.
And from there the Sultan came to Mosul,
and he gave it to Sayf al-Dawlah Ibrahim,
his uterine brother.
And he was a just man.
For a certain tax-collector from Mosul came to him and said
that he would give him every day a hundred gold dinars from the dues of those who buy and sell in the market.
And he gathered the leaders of the people of Mosul and said to them:
"Do you desire this tax-collector?" And they answered:
"If you relieve us from the Persian executioners and the Ghuzz extortioners,
we are pleased with this one who is from among us."
And Sayf al-Dawlah showed magnanimity and said:
"I will relieve you even from this one;
and we do not seek from you more than the dues on the harvests and the fruits of the earth in their season."
And he commanded the heralds,
and they proclaimed the exemption of those who buy and sell.
And all the people raised their voices
and prayed for the length of his life.
And from Mosul the Sultan went down to Baghdad.
And when he drew near to the city,
the Caliph sent the vizier, the chief of chiefs, to meet him.
And he presented to the Sultan a Khosroan cup of gold,
and in it were precious stones: rubies, emeralds, and sapphire.
And he said:
"The Commander of the Faithful rejoiced greatly in your triumph,
and was comforted by your approach,"
and other such things.
The Sultan, however, gave thanks and said:
"I am a servant who gives satisfaction to this court,
and a recipient of the great favors that have been poured out upon me from it.
And henceforth I lack nothing
except to meet and be honored by his prophetic sight;
and I can no longer bear to be deprived of it."
And the vizier replied:
"Henceforth there is no obstacle,
because you have become one household,
and you have been mingled and blended with one another,"
that is to say, by intermarriage.
And the vizier arose and went in to the Caliph
and informed him of these things.
And the Sultan also entered his new palace which he had built.
